head: 8dfc8c90135f5821f35849d8f61a4a21db1d50c9
summary:
This is a stale re-read of the tree at 8dfc8c9. All three findings sent back from earlier rounds are fixed in the code.

- **M1 (harness plant rows):** Planting._create now writes over an existing file that is listed under awaiting_file, saving its bytes in saved and manifest, and restore() writes them back and checks their SHA-256. There is a single caller of Planting, at harness.py:699. tests/bugs/SL-107-HarnessPlantsOverRecord.Tests.py passed 4/4 in 0.04 s under the engine venv and left no __pycache__ behind. It runs the real rows S83-S86 and P36: they plant over an existing record and put it back, they create and remove the record when it is absent, and a file not in awaiting_file is still PLANT-BROKEN.
- **m1 (one code-363 rule):** the doc now gives one rule. The Q-261 list, section 4, row (d) and the result table all say 'equal to the same-session Temp anchor's code-363 count', with a sentence that this replaces Q-261's fixed range for that count only.
- **R2-m2 (UTF-8 capture):** the UTF-8 console line now comes before the tee, with a paragraph saying why.

HandOffCases C-003 passed, including the new ordering check and the check that no fixed 27-28 pass range is left. RuleCases.ps1 was edited and then reverted (net zero), and WindowCases.ps1, fitness.yaml and SL-089-seams.md are unchanged since the last review.

New this round:
- **A wrong follow-up (minor defect, filed below).** The build's follow-up says the awaiting_file entry 'can be dropped; the harness works either way'. That is now false: awaiting_file is exactly what lets the five rows write over the record, so dropping it brings back five PLANT-BROKEN rows (Q-027 makes this harness run a required check at later slices' validate).
- **Design record reverted (drift, not a finding).** Build attempt 2 committed the engine's re-exported design-slice-1.json, which has would_force_resynthesis true and the first-draft pattern. So O-015 is not true of the tree, despite the build's account. A file edit cannot discharge it (Q-106): the engine's export overwrites the file on refresh.

Second round: This round tried to break the code changed since 7c3dc31 and found nothing new.

**Planting._create, the branch that writes over an existing record:**
- It saves the original bytes and SHA-256 before it writes, so a failed write or a PLANT-BROKEN row after the write still puts the record back through restore().
- Each new-file row gets its own batch, so two rows never touch the record in one batch.
- It is not added to created, so restore() never deletes the person's record.
- copy_tree uses shutil.copyfile, so a read-only attribute or a link on the person's record does not reach the scratch copy.
- The path is compared in lower case. The only casing mismatch would be a hand-renamed record, which makes the harness exit 2 at restore() rather than pass falsely, and Write-W001Record always writes exactly c-drive-run.json.
- harness.py:699 is the only caller of the new Planting signature.

**The other changes:**
- tests/bugs/SL-107-HarnessPlantsOverRecord.Tests.py loads the real rows and the real awaiting_file entry, and writes no bytecode.
- The HandOffCases C-003 additions find the first 'Tee-Object -FilePath artifacts' at the doc's command line, after the UTF-8 line, and the negative check covers all three old fixed-range spellings.
- The UTF-8 console line uses a no-BOM encoding and affects only how the window decodes the run's output, which round 2's simulation showed keeps a non-ASCII path intact.
- The anchor runs are not teed, but nothing is lost: they write straight to the console (now UTF-8), and a bounded anchor can be re-run cheaply if it leaks.

The earlier rounds' items stand as filed: the false awaiting_file follow-up (R3-m1) and the reverted design record (drift).

findings.claim: Build attempt 2's follow-up says 'Once the person's record is committed, the awaiting_file entry in plants.json can be dropped; the harness works either way'. The index lists it as an open issue headed for the backlog. It is false since this build's own M1 fix. measure() builds Planting's awaiting_files from load_awaiting(plants.json) (harness.py:699), and Planting._create writes over an existing record only when its path is in that set (harness.py:403). Drop the entry after the person commits the record, as the follow-up says, and S83, S84, S85, S86 and P36 return to PLANT-BROKEN ('already exists, so it cannot be created'). Every full harness run then exits 1, at the validate of every later slice that touches fitness.yaml (Q-027). That is the defect M1 fixed. Only the out-of-band test tests/bugs/SL-107-HarnessPlantsOverRecord.Tests.py would notice (test_the_rows_are_all_there_and_all_at_the_awaiting_file asserts the record is listed, and test_a_file_that_is_not_awaited_is_still_plant_broken shows the consequence); no routine gate runs it.

quote.text: "issue": "Once the person's record is committed, the awaiting_file entry in plants.json can be dropped; the harness works either way."

findings.fix: Withdraw that follow-up and replace it with: 'awaiting_file must stay while plants.json has rows that plant .taad/slices/SL-089/c-drive-run.json: it lets the clean baseline pass while the record is absent, and lets those rows write over the record once it exists.' Add the second half of that sentence to the awaiting_file part of plants.json's _note.

obligations.evidence: Owed to validate and dependent on the person's run. Section 5 of docs/design/SL-107-c-drive-run.md gives each item a measurement or a stated bound: (a) is bounded only from below and called unmeasurable, and (f) is measured by the same-session Temp anchor.

Parts (2) to (4) are in the tree: the doc's reason section, WindowCases.ps1 unchanged, and only the two planned sentences in SL-089-seams.md. Part (1) is the design-record flag, and at HEAD the file says would_force_resynthesis true (design-slice-1.json:465). See O-015.

At HEAD 8dfc8c9, .taad/slices/SL-107/design-slice-1.json:465 says would_force_resynthesis true, and line 151 holds the first-draft pattern. Build attempt 2 committed the engine's re-export, contrary to its own account. A build-stage file edit cannot discharge this: Q-106 says the file is an export of the engine's design payload and is overwritten on refresh. Sending it back to build would loop; it needs the engine's design record, or a decision that O-002's recorded discharge is enough.
